q:
In a quadratic function, the value of the product of the roots (α, β) is 4. Find the value of

(α^n + β^n) / (α^-n + β^-n)
explanation: α^-n + β^-n = (α^n + β^n)/(αβ)^n, so the ratio (α^n+β^n)/(α^-n+β^-n) simplifies to (αβ)^n = 4^n, since the product of the roots αβ = 4.

q: Choose the correct expression for f(x) given in the graph, which peaks at (1, 2), passes through (-3, -2), and reaches 0 at x = 3.

explanation: The graph peaks at (1,2) and is linear (a V-shape flipped, i.e. a tent) on either side, reaching 0 at x=3 and -2 at x=-3. f(x) = 2 - |x-1| gives f(1)=2, f(3)=2-2=0, and f(-3)=2-4=-2, matching all three points, so option (C) is correct.

q:
The width of the physical address on a machine is 40 bits. The width of the tag field in a 512 KB 8-way set associative cache is _______ bits.

(As printed, the question does not state a block/line size; the official answer key's value of 24 corresponds to the standard version of this question with a cache block size of 32 bytes.)
explanation: With a 32-byte block size: number of lines = 512KB/32B = 2^14, number of sets = 2^14/8 = 2^11, so offset = 5 bits and index = 11 bits, leaving tag = 40 - 5 - 11 = 24 bits, matching the official key.

q:
A file system uses an in-memory cache to cache disk blocks. The miss rate of the cache is shown in the figure. The latency to read a block from the cache is 1 ms and to read a block from the disk is 10 ms. Assume that the cost of checking whether a block exists in the cache is negligible. Available cache sizes are in multiples of 10 MB.

The smallest cache size required to ensure an average read latency of less than 6 ms is ________ MB.
figure: <svg viewBox="0 0 340 300" width="100%" style="max-width:420px;height:auto" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><g stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1" fill="none"><line x1="40" y1="20" x2="40" y2="260"/><line x1="40" y1="260" x2="320" y2="260"/></g><polyline points="71,47 102,100 133,153 164,167 196,180 227,193 258,207 289,220" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5"/><g fill="currentColor"><circle cx="71" cy="47" r="2.5"/><circle cx="102" cy="100" r="2.5"/><circle cx="133" cy="153" r="2.5"/><circle cx="164" cy="167" r="2.5"/><circle cx="196" cy="180" r="2.5"/><circle cx="227" cy="193" r="2.5"/><circle cx="258" cy="207" r="2.5"/><circle cx="289" cy="220" r="2.5"/></g><g font-size="9" fill="currentColor" text-anchor="middle"><text x="71" y="272">10</text><text x="102" y="272">20</text><text x="133" y="272">30</text><text x="164" y="272">40</text><text x="196" y="272">50</text><text x="227" y="272">60</text><text x="258" y="272">70</text><text x="289" y="272">80</text></g><g font-size="9" fill="currentColor" text-anchor="end"><text x="35" y="24">90</text><text x="35" y="103">60</text><text x="35" y="183">30</text><text x="35" y="263">0</text></g><text x="180" y="290" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" text-anchor="middle">Cache size (MB)</text><text x="15" y="140" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" text-anchor="middle" transform="rotate(-90 15 140)">Miss rate (%)</text></svg>
explanation: Average latency = missrate×10 + (1-missrate)×1 = 1 + 9×missrate, which must be < 6 ms, i.e. missrate < 5/9 ≈ 55.6%. From the graph, 20 MB gives a 60% miss rate (avg 6.4 ms, too slow), but 30 MB gives a 40% miss rate (avg 4.6 ms), so the smallest sufficient cache size is 30 MB.
